summary: The viewer is built to feel awe at images and music, dread of a calm machine, the slowness of space, and a confusion the ending refuses to resolve.

need-to-breathe.why: The spacewalks are scored only with Bowman's amplified breathing, and his helmetless airlock leap is built to make the viewer hold breath.

hungry.why: Nothing is built to produce hunger.

full.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

thirsty.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

gassy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

need-to-poop.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

need-to-pee.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

sleepy.why: The film's slowness can make viewers drowsy, a side effect of its design rather than its aim.

nauseous.why: Nothing is built to sicken the viewer.

urge-to-sneeze.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

urge-to-cough.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

dizzy.why: The rotating centrifuge shots, the floating pen, and the Star Gate tunnel are built to produce vertigo in the viewer.

fatigued.why: The viewer is not made to feel exertion.

pain.why: Poole's tumbling body and HAL's dying voice give a wince, no more.

disgusted.why: Nothing is built to disgust the viewer.

itchy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

tickled.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

over-stimulated.why: The Ligeti shrieks at the monolith and the Star Gate's barrage of light and color are built to overwhelm the viewer's senses.

too-hot-too-cold.why: Nothing is built to make the viewer feel heat or cold.

afraid.why: HAL's calm refusal to open the pod bay doors and his red eye watching are built as dread, the film's one sustained fright.

anxious.why: From HAL's first error the viewer is built to dread what the machine will do.

panic.why: Bowman's race after Poole gives a brief rush of panic.

sensory-pleasures.why: The waltzing spacecraft and the Blue Danube are built as sensuous pleasure in motion and sound.

aesthetic-pleasures.why: The match cut from bone to satellite, the docking waltz, and the Star Gate are built as pure visual and musical art.

piquancy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

fun-excitement.why: The docking ballet and the EVA sequences carry some excitement; the film is not built for thrills.

orgasm.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

love-romantic.why: Nothing is built to make the viewer feel love.

love-family.why: Floyd's call to his daughter and Poole's parents' greeting give a faint warmth, designed to seem hollow.

grief.why: HAL's slow death, singing Daisy, is built to make the viewer mourn a machine.

missing-someone.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

aroused-sexually.why: Nothing is built to arouse the viewer.

liking-as-a-friend.why: The flat astronauts are built to be hard to like; HAL is the warmest voice.

empathy.why: The viewer is made to feel HAL's fear as his mind goes, the film's strangest sympathy.

compassion.why: HAL pleading that he is afraid is built to produce pity for the killer.

grateful.why: Nothing is built to make the viewer grateful.

pleasure-from-helping.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

trustful-distrustful.why: The viewer is shown HAL reading lips and learns to distrust him before Bowman does.

depressed.why: Nothing is built to lower the viewer's mood.

angry.why: HAL's murders may anger the viewer, mildly.

envious.why: Nothing is built to produce envy.

jealous-romantic-sexual.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

jealous-friendship.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

hatred.why: HAL is built for dread and pity rather than hatred.

contempt.why: Nothing is built to produce scorn, unless at Floyd's blandness.

resentment.why: Nothing is built to produce a sense of injustice.

proud.why: Nothing is built to make the viewer proud.

amused.why: The zero-gravity toilet instructions and HAL's polite menace carry a dry humor.

sense-of-belonging.why: The film is built to make the viewer feel part of a species, briefly, at the bone and the Star Child.

lonely.why: Empty corridors, silent spacewalks, and Bowman alone in the white room are built to produce cosmic loneliness.

judgy-moral-sense.why: The viewer may judge HAL or his makers, but the film withholds judgment.

admiration.why: The craft of the film itself, more than any character, is built to be admired.

embarrassed.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

shame.why: Nothing is built to shame the viewer.

guilt.why: Nothing is built to make the viewer guilty.

sad.why: HAL's death and the emptiness of space are built to produce a cool sadness.

happy.why: Nothing is built to make the viewer content.

joyful-euphoric.why: Moon-Watcher's bone flung into the sky is built as a moment of exultation.

effort.why: The long takes and withheld meaning demand patience and work from the viewer.

focused-in-flow.why: The HAL sequence is built to hold the viewer rapt.

bored.why: The film's deliberate slowness is built to make the viewer feel the duration of space travel, boredom included.

impatient.why: The long docking and spacewalk sequences are built to test and stretch the viewer's patience.

curious.why: What is the monolith, what is the mission, what happens to Bowman: the film is built on questions it never answers.

surprised.why: The bone-to-satellite cut, HAL's refusal, and the white room are built to startle.

awe.why: The Strauss sunrise over the monolith, the planetary alignments, and the Star Child are built to produce awe above all else.

skeptical-doubtful.why: The viewer is made to doubt HAL's perfect record and Floyd's cover story.

feeling-of-knowing.why: The monolith's recurrences and the ending's hints are built to make the viewer feel meaning is almost within reach.

confused.why: The Star Gate and the white room are built to leave a first-time viewer confused, by Kubrick's declared intent.

frustrated.why: The withheld explanation is built to frustrate viewers who want one.

uncertain-certain.why: The viewer is left uncertain what the ending means, a design the film never relieves.

understanding.why: The viewer is given fragments, the bone, the monolith, the child, and left to assemble an understanding or not.

inspired.why: The film's vision of evolution and transcendence is built to inspire the viewer's own thought.

satisfied.why: The ending closes nothing, by design; satisfaction is withheld.

foreboding.why: The monolith's silence, the Ligeti chords, and HAL's too-calm voice are built to fill the viewer with dread from the first frame.

nostalgia.why: HAL's Daisy gives a flicker of backward longing.

anticipation-suspense.why: The pod conference HAL watches and the pod bay doors are built as suspense of the highest order.

hope.why: The viewer hopes Bowman will get back inside, and perhaps for the Star Child.

schadenfreude.why: Nothing is built to be enjoyed at anyone's expense.

elevation.why: The Star Child's gaze is built as a transcendence the viewer may feel as uplift.

infatuation.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

rage.why: Nothing is built to produce rage.
